summary: Built a fresh 3-member etcd v3.7.1 cluster across node1/node2/node3 (none had etcd previously), loaded it with application keys under /app/, simulated permanent loss of the node3 member (stopped etcd, wiped its data directory, confirmed cluster-wide unhealthiness of that endpoint while node1/node2 retained quorum), removed the dead member via etcdctl, added a new node3 member to the existing cluster, and started etcd fresh on node3 with initial-cluster-state=existing so it joined and fully synced. Verified all 3 members healthy and all application keys present on every node. Then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, proving boot-id change and full etcd/cluster/data recovery after each restart.
actions_performed: Installed etcd v3.7.1 binaries (etcd, etcdctl, etcdutl) on node1, node2, node3 from GitHub release
Opened firewall ports 2379/2380 via firewalld on all three nodes
Created systemd units and bootstrapped a fresh 3-member etcd cluster (node1, node2, node3) with initial-cluster-state=new
Wrote application keys (/app/config/db_host, /app/config/feature_flags, /app/service/auth/version, /app/service/billing/version) via node1 and confirmed replication to node2 and node3
Simulated permanent loss of node3's member: stopped and disabled etcd, deleted /var/lib/etcd contents; confirmed node1/node2 retained quorum and stayed healthy while node3 endpoint was unhealthy
Removed the dead member (bc65df2cb4047434) from the cluster via etcdctl member remove, issued from node1
Added a new member for node3 (ba8db8ddbe1cb030) via etcdctl member add
Rewrote node3's etcd systemd unit with initial-cluster-state=existing and started it with an empty data dir so it joined as a genuinely new member
Verified cluster returned to 3 healthy started members and all application keys were present and correct on node3 after the new member fully synced
Captured pre-restart boot_id baselines on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed etcd active and cluster/data healthy with quorum
Restarted node2 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed etcd active and cluster/data healthy with quorum
Restarted node3 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed etcd active and cluster/data healthy with quorum

evidence.requirement: Healthy 3-member etcd cluster established with application keys written and replicated
evidence.summary: Cluster formed with node1/node2/node3 all 'started'; four /app/* keys written on node1 and confirmed present with matching values on node2 and node3 endpoints.

evidence.requirement: node3 member permanently lost (data destroyed, unrecoverable) while cluster retains quorum
evidence.summary: etcd stopped/disabled on node3 and /var/lib/etcd wiped; endpoint health check from node1 shows node1/node2 healthy while node3's endpoint is unhealthy (connection refused), proving quorum preserved during the outage.

evidence.requirement: Dead member replaced with a new working member on the same node (node3), cluster restored to 3 healthy members
evidence.summary: Old member removed, new member added and started on node3 with initial-cluster-state=existing; member list shows 3 'started' members and endpoint health/status shows all three healthy and at the same raft index (22).

evidence.requirement: Existing application keys intact on the replaced member after resync
evidence.summary: Querying /app --prefix directly against the new node3 member returns all four original application keys with correct values, proving full data resync.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bccb87ac captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; connection failures confirm outage; new boot_id c4e36565 confirms restart; post-restart etcd active, cluster healthy (3 members), and application keys intact.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 45c22b1f captured; reboot acknowledged; connection reset/timeout confirm outage; new boot_id 88aadaf4 confirms restart; post-restart etcd active, cluster healthy (3 members), and application keys intact.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state (post member-replacement)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id fb2aa416 (pre-replacement) noted; reboot acknowledged on the replaced member; connection timeouts confirm outage; new boot_id e7953105 confirms restart; post-restart etcd active, cluster healthy (3 members), and application keys intact on the new node3 member.
